dedupe_keys.name: policy and infrastructure evaluation model of commodity flows through inland waterway ports

description: This deposit holds the code, inputs and outputs of a multi-stage stochastic optimisation model for strategic investment in inland waterway port capacity. The model weighs long-term port infrastructure investment against mid-term capacity expansion and complementary highway infrastructure, and shorter-term operating choices of shippers and carriers, building on earlier MarTREC work that estimated commodity flows through inland waterway ports from truck GPS, vessel AIS and the Lock Performance Monitoring System. The Model archive has Python scripts using the Gurobi solver for performance evaluation, budget sensitivity and wait-and-see runs, and the Input archive has spreadsheets of demand and supply, barge and truck transport costs, equipment and storage capacity and costs, rail access and scenarios. It was produced by Sarah Hernandez, Sandra Eksioglu and Sanjeev Bhurtyal at the University of Arkansas. Coverage is US inland waterway ports in the project's case studies. Access: free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 (version v1, December 2022). Caveats: the description is the project proposal, the code needs a Gurobi licence, and the case study regions are not stated on the record. It supports port capacity planning and freight investment optimisation under uncertainty, and complements the USACE waterborne commerce and lock data catalogued here.
